page: Vultr vcg-a100-96c-960g-640vram is a server instance within the Dedicated Metal GPU family, built on the Intel x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 96 shared vCPUs paired with 960.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 10:1, this configuration is structurally aligned with memory-intensive workloads. The shared CPU allocation model suggests that while the instance offers massive memory capacity and fast NVMe local storage, CPU resources are shared, which may introduce variable processing performance under sustained multi-core loads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory and storage density relative to the shared CPU allocation makes this server type suitable for workloads requiring large datasets in memory without requiring constant, dedicated maximum CPU performance.

Appropriate workloads for this hardware profile include large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, big data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. The 2200 GB NVMe SSD provides the necessary high-speed local storage to support fast read and write operations for database logging and temporary data staging.
